column1: Post‑COVID Inflation & the Monetary Policy Dilemma: An Agent‑Based Scenario Analysis

The thesis titled Post-COVID Inflation & the Monetary Policy Dilemma: An Agent-Based Scenario Analysis by Max Sina Knicker  Karl Naumann-Woleske  Jean-Philippe Bouchaud  and Francesco Zamponi  explores the complex dynamics of inflation in the aftermath of the COVID-19 pandemic using an agent-based modeling approach. The authors employ the Mark-0 Agent-Based Model to simulate the economic environment from 2020 to 2023  focusing on how economic agents  guided by behavioral rules  respond to various shocks and policy interventions. A key feature of the model is the inclusion of a mechanism that allows the trust of economic agents in the Central Bank to de-anchor  reflecting real-world uncertainties.

The study examines the impact of three significant exogenous shocks that occurred during the pandemic: a production/consumption shock due to lockdowns  a supply-chain shock  and an energy price shock  the latter exacerbated by geopolitical tensions such as the Russian invasion of Ukraine. By analyzing these shocks under different monetary policy scenarios  the authors aim to understand the resurgence of inflation in the United States  considering factors like demand-pull  cost-push  and profit-driven inflation.

The findings of the study are multifaceted. Firstly  without appropriate fiscal policy interventions  the economy could take years to recover from these shocks  with the risk of falling into a deep recession. Secondly  the effectiveness of monetary policy in controlling inflation is largely attributed to the anchoring of expectations rather than the direct impact of interest rate changes. However  the study also highlights a paradox: strong inflation anchoring can negatively affect consumption and employment  creating a narrow window for optimal policy responses due to the trade-off between inflation and unemployment. Lastly  the model identifies wage and price indexation as the most sensitive parameters  indicating their critical role in inflation dynamics.

The implications of this research are significant for Central Bank decision-making  providing a tool to anticipate the outcomes of various monetary and fiscal policies. The study underscores the importance of expectation management and the delicate balance required in policy formulation to navigate post-COVID economic challenges effectively.
